Use case: background-extraction / precise-object-edit.
Asset type: one transparent production sprite for the existing Godot pixel-art town, not concept art.
Reference: the attached snowy hamlet concept. Extract and faithfully recreate ONLY its central circular stone bonfire and the low paved gathering apron beneath it, as an isolated game sprite.
Subject: thick low circular ring of weathered gray-brown stone blocks, visible front wall and open top, stacked blackened timber, bright ivory-yellow flame core and copper-orange tongues. Small snow remnants on outer paving. Two short empty timber benches at the far left and far right of the paving, kept subordinate and inside the sprite bounds. No people.
Camera: same high three-quarter top-down game view as the reference, almost orthographic, circular floor projects as a wide shallow ellipse. Match the concept's pixel clusters, muted slate/old copper/ivory palette, crisp un-antialiased texture. Flame is luminous with detailed readable structure, not a flat icon or outline. Keep a compact silhouette that stays readable displayed at roughly 120 by 90 game pixels.
Composition: a single centered asset, width about 80% of canvas and height about 75%; complete silhouette with clear transparent padding. Hearth centered in the lower middle, fire tips fully within bounds. No huge shadows, no atmospheric background, no buildings, no UI, no text, no logos, no grid and no checkerboard painted into the image. Output true alpha transparency. All outside pixels transparent.
